We strive to have a learning culture where we aspire for success for every member, where thinking, problem solving and risk taking are encouraged.
We are committed to giving our best in all we do to ensure our children are prepared for the future, both through engaging, meaningful education and by developing confidence, self-belief and resilience.

We will create a community where values are shared and respect is integral; a community where each individual is understood, nurtured, kept safe and celebrated.
We will reflect and research to ensure we constantly move forward in giving our children equal opportunities and the highest quality education that they deserve.
A journey to success where barriers are only hurdles to be overcome and challenges stimulate our learning.

After originally joining the school as deputy in 2012. I feel privileged to serve as head teacher of Corbets Tey School
My teaching career began in a Thurrock special school as soon as I finished my BEd (Hons) and I remain committed to improving outcomes for all students who have additional needs.
At Corbets Tey I enjoyed setting up specialist classes and helping the school to gain its specialist status for communication and interaction. I am proud of our approaches to ensuring every student develops a functional communication system.
I am passionate about raising levels of aspiration and achievement for students of all abilities. In our school I am committed to developing a culture in which initial barriers to learning are perceived as a stimulus for seeking the solutions to success.
My husband, Steve, also teaches students with additional needs and I have two grown up sons.

Corbets Tey School
A Specialist College for Communication and Interaction
About Us
Main Site in Upminster (for students aged 4 to 16)
Post 16 Site in Rainham (for students aged 16 to 19)
Corbets Tey School is a school for students with Complex Learning Needs
The school is a state maintained, foundation special school situated in Upminster, Essex in the south east of the London Borough of Havering. Up to 155 children and young people attend the school aged 4 to 19, all with Education, Health and Care Plans detailing educational needs including communication and interaction difficulties, Autism and medical syndromes and physical and sensory needs. There are two sites with Pre-16 students at the main site in Upminster and Post 16 students at the CTS @ The Avelon provision in Rainham.
The school was awarded Specialist Status in Communication and Interaction in 2007, successfully re-designating in 2010. An internal specialist department was established alongside individual language and communication programmes. The school continues to support behaviour, assessment and language and communication development work in other schools within Havering.
Governors and staff at the school have high expectations for students to achieve their best in terms of their independence, social and moral development, as well as their academic achievement, so that they may ultimately make a valuable contribution to society and to prepare them for a fulfilling and purposeful adult life.
Students can be admitted at any time during the academic year but it is usual for the school to have its full complement by the beginning of the school academic year. All students coming to the school have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP).

Corbets Tey School
A Specialist College for Communication and Interaction
Curriculum Overviews
Click on the links on the right to learn more about the curriculum in each phase group and about communication within the curriculum.
Any further information on the school curriculum can be sought by contacting the school office.
Our curriculum caters for students in Reception to Year 14.
We are continuing to develop our curriculum offer within progression pathways in line with the National Curriculum.
Teachers plan from the Early Years and National Curriculum year expectations which are accessible and appropriate to the students within their classes. The curriculum is a vehicle of enrichment to teach hierarchical, personalised skills which become functional for life as children and young people progress within developmental pathways through the school.
We aim to ensure that our pupils are 100% engaged in their learning and this aspiration leads our curriculum development. We are continually learning what motivates and engages our students and this is illustrated through increased multi-sensory and active learning in lessons.
We ensure pupils have regular opportunities for physical exercise in addition to timetabled PE and swimming﻿
The curriculum is delivered in classes through a topic based approach. Objectives are individual and specific to the communication and behavioural needs of students. There are six main school topics intersperse d with mini topics that last between one and two weeks.
The Incredible Journey
Throughout the school, for some students the key focus will be on further developing functional communication and independence skills. For others the key focus will be on ensuring the highest academic qualifications as a passport to access to mainstream courses at a later stage in college.
We are committed to considering the most appropriate pathways for each individual student and work in partnership with students, parents and carers to ensure common goals and aspiration.﻿

pageCache.pageTitle: Adverse Weather at Corbets Tey School
pageCache.text:
Corbets Tey School
A Specialist College for Communication and Interaction
Adverse Weather or School Closure
Weather Updates and Alerts
Nothing extraordinary to report at present...
Our intentions with regard to inclement weather are:
Open Check is an easy-to-use service that will tell you if the school is open or closed in case of emergency, severe weather or any news which may affect children’s ability to attend or access the school. OpenCheck is also available via ParentComms:Mobile as an app available for all popular smart phones, ensuring that Parents and carers have a choice of options for keeping up to date.
The school policy is that we will aim to keep the school open if at all possible but safety of students and staff will always be a primary consideration in this.
As many students travel to school using community transport, their decision on whether to run the transport service will affect the numbers of students attending school during adverse weather. A small number of students also travel to school by car and public transport and parents/carers will be able to make their own decision with regard to the safety of bringing their children to school.
The severity of the weather and how many staff can get to school will impact on our ability to stay open. Many of our staff travel quite long distances and from fairly remote areas and so their ability to get to school will affect this.
Our main considerations in remaining open will be:
As we may be unable to determine these factors by the time the children leave home on school buses, we may have to decide to close the school later in the morning if we do not have adequate staffing. Therefore, in deciding to place your child on the school bus in the morning, you should be aware that you may be required to collect your child if the school cannot remain open.
As the school operates on two sites, Harwood Hall Lane and Avelon Road (including CT@TA Post 16 and Routes 4 Life Post 19 provisions), closure decisions may be made separately and independently based on the conditions and staffing levels and any other factors affecting each site. Separate decisions will therefore be made and communicated for both sites.
We would urge you to regularly check the school website as we will post information here via the Open Check link. If you do not have access to the Internet, please try to obtain contact details of someone who can check this for you. ﻿

Corbets Tey School
A Specialist College for Communication and Interaction
Language Resource Centre
Specialist School Status
In September 2007, Corbets Tey School gained Specialist Status for Communication and Interaction and successfully re-designated in 2010. This enabled us to develop our Language work both internally for our own pupils and externally for Mainstream Schools and other partners. We spent our ‘Capital Build’ allocation on a new wing which provides a Language Resource and Advice Centre, Training room and Partnership offices on the first floor.
Language Advice and Resource Centre
at Corbets Tey School, Harwood Hall Lane, Upminster RM14 2YQ
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Educational Support Service (SEND ESS)
Open Every Wednesday Afternoon
The Language Resource and Advice Centre is open to all Havering schools and pre-school settings every Wednesday afternoon during term time from 1.30pm-4.30pm.
Advice and support are available each week from an Advisory Teacher and Communication & Interaction Education Advisor, for children and young people in your school or setting. Advice and support with implementing Speech and Language report recommendations is also available.
A wide range of resources are available for you to borrow free of charge, to assist in the delivery of speech, language, and communication programmes or SLT care plans for use in your school or setting.
We aim to be as user friendly as possible and therefore have technology-based language support resources e.g. Black Sheep Press, Widgit and Clicker as well as resource making equipment such as printers and laminators for your use.
New resources are purchased in line with the needs of schools, so any suggestions for latest items to be added to the library are welcome.
Demonstrations and Modelling
Colleagues will be available to model how the following strategies and interventions can be used to support children in your school, or setting:
Please let us know in advance by emailing SENDeducation@havering.gov.uk if you would like to access a modelling session to enable the team to prepare accordingly.
Where possible, please park off site as parking at Corbets Tey School is very limited. For safety reasons, please avoid arriving/leaving the car park during the school bus times between 2.15-3.00pm.

pageCache.pageTitle: Forms and Information for Parents and Carers at Corbets Tey School
pageCache.text:
Corbets Tey School
A Specialist College for Communication and Interaction
Permission Forms and Information Sheets
In our school, we aim to have clear and effective communications with all parents and carers. Effective communications enable us to share our aims and values, through keeping parents and carers well informed about school life. This reinforces the important role that parents and carers play in supporting the school and their child or young person’s learning.
Parents and carers are always welcome to see their child or young person’s class teacher to discuss progress by pre-arranged appointment. Parents and carers who come to the school must sign-in at reception on arrival.
If required, an appointment can be made to see the Head Teacher or Deputy Headteacher if there are any unresolved issues.
Good communication between the school and the home is essential; children and young people achieve more when schools, parents and carers work together. The school encourages parents and carers to share any issues about their child or young person at the earliest opportunity.
How we Communicate
Permission Forms
Applications and Agreements
Home/School Diaries
A daily dialogue between class teacher and home is important to ensure that relevant information is relayed each day to parents and carers who can respond or provide information about their child or young person.
Each class teacher or tutor designs an effective method of home-school communication suitable for the needs of their class, students, parents and carers. This is to ensure that they are as student-centred as possible.
Parents of younger students may find a diary page with symbol supports useful to aid discussion between parents and carers and their young people. These can be used as a prompt for parents and carers to communicate with their child or young person about their activities and feelings on how their day went.
Some parents and carers may prefer a daily communication by email or a paper diary sent home in students’ bags.
Telephone
Parents and carers are welcome to telephone the school with urgent messages that need to be delivered immediately to staff. Urgent calls may be put through to the most appropriate or available person.
If it is not possible for a parent or carer to speak to class staff, a message will be taken and delivered for contact to be made within a reasonable time. Non-urgent calls to class staff should be kept to a minimum at times of the day where teaching and learning may be disrupted. This includes before school where lessons are being prepared.
Texts and Emails
It is preferred that parents and carers do not contact staff by text.
Parents and carers should not expect staff to:
Return calls after work hours
Answer email in the evening or weekends
Home/School Agreement
Since March 2015, a Home School Agreement is not a statutory requirement for schools. However, the school still values the use of a Home School Agreement, which sets out the school’s responsibilities towards students, the responsibilities of parents and carers and what the school expects of students. It is designed to help achieve a supportive, communicative and effective partnership and is sent to parents and carers annually.
Newsletters
The school sends regular newsletters to parents and carers. It contains general details of school events and activities. We send other letters of a general nature when necessary.
Parent/Carer Surveys
The school distributes a parent and carer survey once in the Summer Term each year to establish the views and opinions of parents and carers on the school performance. This is analysed by senior management and governors and this data is used to provide a focus for wellbeing initiatives and school improvement.
School Website
Our school website has up to date information on the school and links to various policies for parents and carers and also includes progress on equality plans and how we are spending Pupil Premium and Primary PE Funding.
Annual Reviews
All students have an annual review to evaluate and develop an action plan regarding all aspects of the student’s life with a view to updating their Education Health Care Plan (EHCP) as appropriate. In Year 9 students, participate in a person centred review which will have contributions from our Educational Psychologist and Careers adviser. Representation from all professional services working with the family can be invited to attend as appropriate.
Parent and Carer Meetings
Parents and carers are invited to at least one meeting per year to discuss their child's progress.
Annual Reports
In the Summer Term, the school provides an annual written report to parents and carers on their child or young person’s progress. This includes information on students’ Learning Pathways (if applicable), individual skills achieved as well as any other additional assessments, and it will be maintained with progress updated throughout the year.

pageCache.text:
Corbets Tey School
A Specialist College for Communication and Interaction
Education and Health and Care Plan (EHCP)
All prospective parents and carers wishing for their child or young perosn to attend Corbets Tey School or Corbets Tey School at the Avelon at Post 16 must have an Education and Health Care Plan (EHCP) in progress (draft) or finalised.
If the student resides in the London Borough of Havering?
Contact Havering’s Assessment and Placement Team on 01708 431885 and speak to your allocated case officer to state that you wish to consult for a placement at one of our settings.
Alternatively parents and carers can wait till their child or young person's next annual review and request a change of placement during the review but should still seek advice from their allocated case officer before doing this
If the student resides in another Borough?
Contact your local authority SEND department and speak to your allocated case officer to state that you wish to consult for a placement at one of our settings.
Alternatively parents and carers can wait till their child or young person's next annual review and request a change of placement during the review but should still seek advice from their allocated case officer before doing this
What happens next?
The Havering Assessment and Placement Team will consult with us directly regarding the possibility of placement.
All consultations from local authorities outside of Havering should be emailed directly to the school via the email address: office@corbetstey.havering.sch.uk and copied to the Havering Assessment and Placement Team (sen@havering.gov.uk)
How do we make a decision?
We will thoroughly look over the consultation paperwork and prepare a response to Havering.
They will forward it on to the appropriate local authority where the initial request originated from

pageCache.text:
Corbets Tey School
A Specialist College for Communication and Interaction
Our Community
John's Journey
John attended Corbets Tey School from the age of eleven and moved on five years later aged sixteen in 2002.
He moved on to attend the Quarles Campus of Havering College. Here he was offered a place on the Rose project, which aimed to secure paid work placements for students with learning difficulties.
In 2008 John was supported by the Rose Project in developing his work skills and then to secure a job back at Corbets Tey School, assisting the site manager.
He was supported, at first by the job coach and then by our site manager Dave, in learning to carry out site duties until he felt confident in his new role. He now takes responsibility for a list of site tasks and he carries these out independently and diligently.
As a result of all of his hard work and determination John has become an asset to the school and carries out his duties to the best of his ability. He is a reliable and sociable member of staff and he always greets other staff professionally and confidently always remembering everyone’s name and more importantly what football team they support!
See a video about John's Journey
Corbets Tey School Reunion
The school organises school reunions every few years to ensure the links between the school and its students remains strong. Leavers usually from the previous 10 years are invited to the school to party and catch up with old friends and staff.
Parents and Friends Association Committee Activity
Corbets Tey School has long counted itself lucky to enjoy the support of an extremely active Parents/Friends Association. The school benefits from an active parental and independent volunteer involvement in both the running of the PFA and assisting in many ways around the school. The school is extremely grateful for this support and hopes it will long continue.
The PFA is a registered charity (number 289742) and its main objective is to advance the education of the pupils of the school by providing and assisting in the provision of facilities, not normally provided by the local education authority. The PFA’s activities include organising fundraising events such as golf days, raffles, sponsored events and gaining support from charitable and grant giving organisations.
Various social functions take place at throughout the year, organised by members of the PFA such as live bands, tribute bands, discos, etc. These events usually attract many parents, friends and staff who, as well as raising funds for the school, have a really great time.
All parents automatically become members of the PFA. If you are interested in becoming more involved in the activities of the Parents and Friends Association, this would be extremely appreciated.
